newsitem.title: BULGARIA: IMF to finalise Bulgaria currency board early 1997.
newsitem.headline: IMF to finalise Bulgaria currency board early 1997.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is expected to finalise talks with Bulgaria on the introduction of a tough monetary regime early next year, an IMF official said on Wednesday.
"We are here to do the technical work needed for the currency board. We want to be ready for negotiations early next year," IMF mission leader Anne McGuirk told reporters on arrival at Sofia airport.

The IMF, which has twice postponed funding for Bulgaria due to the government's failure to meet reform targets, proposed a month ago the implementation of a currency board to restore confidence in the collapsing lev and crumbling economy.
The government had accepted the plan saying the system will be introduced after parliament passes next year's budget and a package of legal amendments which would make the currency board operational.
"We'll be looking into policies needed to support it (the currency board), it is not magic. We'll be discussing the budget and how the central bank needs to be reorganised," said McGuirk.
Under the system, the central bank must not print levs it cannot cover with hard currency reserves. This should remove political pressure from monetary policy.
The bank will also be banned from lending to the government and commercial banks.

The central bank has said some $500 million in reserves plus the strategic gold reserves worth $450 million were enough to comply with a currency board plan but were insufficient to cover pending foreign debt payments of around $300 million due in the first quarter of next year.
Central bank reserves stood at $525.1 million at end-November.

Bulgaria will have access to its maximum annual limit of more than $700 million in IMF loans granted only in extraordinary circumstances and the government was given to understand that it may qualify when it introduces the currency board, bankers said recently.

One of Bulgaria's options is to agree on a currency board implementation timetable with the IMF missions in December and make the necessary legal adjustments in the next one or two months and then introduce the currency board.
The alternative is to make the legal adjustments as soon as possible and introduce the plan in January, the bankers said.

Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said on Monday he hoped parliament would pass the 1997 budget by the end of the year and vote on the legal package on January 2. He said the national assembly would work through its Christmas recess if necessary.
